audits.text:
## 346480121fcb

**Reproduced teaching defect and override-contract defects** at generator SHA-256
`205991c61dab66fdea559684f78266cae122a0943e2ce35c9372ce6ad66f325d`.
The target has no portable task tests and declares no semantic contract, so the
strict combined audit fails explicitly rather than counting absence as a pass.

The concrete rival is: ignore the transform key and return the first
selector-colored body blob unchanged. Four independently generated, self-checking
`easy` inputs all had `key=1`; the rival matched all 4/4 independent canonical
Racket labels. A legal, self-checking `hard` input generated with seed `11`,
sample index `190`, and exact override `key=2` refuted it (0/1 match). Exact
inputs, selected-Racket outputs, source/rule hashes, and the rival comparison are
in `checks/audit/346480121fcb/ignore_key_rival.json` and its referenced files.
Thus an easy-only lesson can teach identity/cropping without teaching the key.

The separate override audit made 47,880 draws and reported 5,332 findings:
unknown keys are accepted; advertised `grid_h`, `grid_w`, and `key` values are
rejected or not observed under parts of the declared matrix; and several palette
or texture values are inert. The minimal probe at seed `137`, sample index `29`,
medium difficulty shows baseline, warm/cool palette, warm/cool texture, an invalid
palette token, and a misspelled axis all accepted with the identical grid hash.
Evidence: `checks/audit/346480121fcb-override/` and
`checks/audit/346480121fcb/override_probe.json`. This was findings-only review;
the audit target was not modified.
